answer: In the EigenTrust graph, each vertex’s score is propagated through normalized peer ratings and reciprocity-weighted transitivity, then discounted by exponential decay with a fixed half-life. Reputation therefore requires sustained honest service. A fresh sybil has negligible incoming trust and near-zero eigenvector centrality; lacking trusted links, it cannot amplify its score or pass consensus, even if a mesa of colluders or a dune of fabricated accounts surrounds it.
